title: Validation of a plain input
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with oracle $\mathcal O$, $r$ a register, $p\in\mathbb Z$, and $c$ a configuration on input $x$. Suppose the transition identities $hU0,hU1,hS,hW0,hWF,hWT,h_1,h_2$ hold at the specified states and none of those states is an oracle-call state, as asserted by $cU0,cU1,cS,cW0,cWF,cWT,c_1,c_2$. Then the run from state $vU0$, input-head position $1$, and register-head position $p$ satisfies the following: if $x$ is a valid plain encoding, it reaches state $next$ at input-head position $1$; if $x$ is not a valid plain encoding, it halts with a rejecting output. In either case, the run preserves the indicated register-head positions and avoids oracle-call states before its endpoint.
